0.content:
Ludi Harpastum (also: Harpastum Festival, Games Harpastum): Ludi Harpastum is one of Mondstadt's oldest festivals, held every year and lasting fifteen days. It is a carnival of songs, wine and flight, the very things Mondstadt takes pride in, and it is especially loved by children. The champion of the games chooses a maiden who, at the climax, throws the Harpastum, a round ball wrapped in red cloth, into the crowd. Whoever catches it is said to enjoy a year of fortune and happiness.

It was founded to remember how the Anemo Archon Barbatos taught people to brew wine and to live freely, and it was meant for everyone. The Latin name means roughly "the Harpastum Games".

Long ago the aristocracy hijacked it, and after Vennessa's rebellion it was restored. In the present day it is a free, public festival again; the manga shows it taking place roughly a year before the main story begins.

Practice: Fifteen days of games, music, food and drink. At the climax a maiden chosen by the champion throws the red-cloth Harpastum ball to the crowd; the person who picks it up is blessed with a year of fortune.

- Games and flight: a gliding championship takes place in the last days of the festival, in the plaza by the Cathedral, according to the Teyvat Travel Highlights text written by a visiting bard.
- Households: each family hangs a handmade Harpastum on the door, made by the lady of the house.
- Food and drink: taverns and restaurants set their best dishes at their doors, Dawn Winery delivers many barrels of beer and cider, and cheese, grilled meat and fresh fruit scent the streets.
- Music: bards come from across the continent and sing poems, and the festivities are said to last all night long.

The same visiting bard says most people have forgotten the original sacred aspect of the festival and treat it as a lively succession of events, but still finds that it shows off Mondstadt's feeling of freedom and independence.

History: Founded to mark Barbatos teaching his people to brew wine and live freely. About a thousand years before the main story the aristocracy that ruled Mondstadt turned it into an elite affair, until Vennessa's rebellion restored it.

Barbatos had left by then, to avoid becoming a tyrant like Decarabian, and the aristocracy had grown corrupt. In the manga's account, the head of the Lawrence Clan, the leading aristocratic family, cancelled all the games and kept only the climax; only his son Barca Lawrence was allowed to touch the ball, anyone else who approached it faced torture, and Barca also claimed the right to take the maiden home. Venti (Barbatos in his travelling form) arrived during the climax. At some point the aristocracy had built a tall tower in the Anemo statue plaza for the maiden to throw from. After the rebellion and the banishment of the aristocracy, the festival returned to its original glory and the tower was taken down.

In the manga, Barca was about to take the ball for the fifth year in a row; the fates of the four earlier maidens are unknown. Venti took the ball himself, fled, and met Vennessa, then an undefeated gladiator belonging to another noble house, who stood up to Barca. The Lawrence Clan later bought Vennessa and her clan and forced her into a gladiator tournament. In the end Venti revealed himself as Barbatos, drove off Ursa the Drake and told Lord Lawrence to hand the city to Vennessa as promised. This is how the manga links the festival to the rebellion; it is not covered in the game's own quests, so treat the details as manga-sourced.

Scene use: Use it for crowded, joyful scenes in Mondstadt: music in the streets, wine and food stalls, children running about, a gliding contest or the red Harpastum ball thrown to the crowd.

Characters may bring up the tradition that catching the ball means a lucky year. In the manga the festival also frames plot: the Fatui are invited to attend, which draws Dottore and Krupp, and Amber takes Collei around the festival after it begins.

Most Mondstadters revere Barbatos without knowing that the bard Venti is the Archon. Do not let a character state the Barca episode as local common knowledge; it is a thousand-year-old story and the aristocracy-era festival is remembered only vaguely, if at all.

Examples: - A child proudly shows a handmade Harpastum hanging on the family door.
- A visiting bard stays for days past their schedule because the festival is too good to leave.
- A knight shows a newcomer around the market until midnight.

- Amber drags a reluctant Collei to the festival to show her what the Anemo Archon's blessing looks like in daily life, as in manga chapter 9.

1.comment: Ludi Harpastum: Harpastum Ball and Maiden
1.content: The Harpastum is a round ball wrapped in red cloth. The champion of the games chooses a maiden, who throws it into the crowd at the climax of Ludi Harpastum, and whoever picks it up is blessed with a year of fortune and happiness. Families also hang handmade Harpastums on their doors. Not to be confused with the Latin ball game harpastum (the name's source) or the Harpastum exploration mechanic.

2.content: Barca Lawrence was the son of Lord Lawrence, head of the aristocratic Lawrence Clan, around the time of Vennessa's rebellion, about a thousand years before the main story. He appears only in the manga Prologue, as an arrogant, spoiled youth who monopolised the Harpastum ball at Ludi Harpastum and took the maiden for himself. After Venti seized the ball, Barca backed down from Vennessa, then the clan took revenge by buying her and her clan. His fate is unknown but presumably he was exiled with his clan.

3.content:
Bards and Music of Mondstadt (also: Mondstadt bards, Bards of Mondstadt, Bardic tradition of Mondstadt): Mondstadt is known as a land of poetry, song and wine, and bards are woven into daily life: they play in the plaza, in taverns and at festivals, and they are paid in Mora or in drinks. The tradition is tied to freedom. In the days of the tyrant Decarabian, songs of resistance were sung in cellars and alleys, and a young bard of Old Mondstadt played his lyre in the rebellion. Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, later took that bard's name and appearance and still wanders the city as the bard Venti.

Bards are ordinary working people in Mondstadt, not courtly figures. They have their own customary dress, rely on audiences' generosity, and compete for good stages. Their songs are also one way Mondstadt keeps its history: the story of the slave Vennessa and the bard god who helped her defeat a drake, and the rebellion against Decarabian, survive in ballads, drinking songs and the text of festival gifts such as Windblume Ode.

Music also has a sacred side. The Church of Favonius keeps the Holy Lyre der Himmel, the instrument Barbatos used, and it is used at Ludi Harpastum. The lyre, the poem and the toast are therefore both entertainment and worship, which is why a bard in Mondstadt can be treated lightly in a tavern and reverently in the cathedral.

Practice: Bards perform on the streets, in squares and in taverns, often for tips or drinks. Inspired travelling bards come to Mondstadt, especially around Ludi Harpastum, and sing poems in the streets.

- Dress: canon shows one bard style for each gender. Men wear a white-and-green striped shirt under a green jacket with green trousers, white boots and a green cravat. Women wear a white blouse and brown skirt under a red dress. Venti's own outfit is a variation on the theme.
- Getting paid: bards earn Mora from onlookers. Venti, as a new arrival, found that no tavern would serve a child-looking customer, so he began playing with a wine cup in his mouth and asking listeners to buy him a drink from the bar instead of giving him Mora. The novelty made him popular. He has a firm rule never to perform where a cat is nearby, since he sneezes at them.

- Popularity: Venti is said to have won the title of Mondstadt's most popular bard three times (recorded on the wiki from the quest That Green Fellow, not traced further).
- Stages: Diluc says bards compete to play at the Angel's Share, his tavern, and takes offence when Venti implies it is not good enough for the Holy Lyre in its worn state.
- Travellers' view: an unnamed bard's diary in the Teyvat Travel Highlights calls Mondstadt the 'Romantic City of Pastorals' and says poetry, music, wine and festivities are the sustenance of a bard's life. The diarist packs 'Select Works of Alan the Bard' and notebooks and pens for the muse, and stayed far longer than planned because of Ludi Harpastum, when bards from all over the continent stop in their tracks to sing poems.
- Taverns as a second home: the same diarist says tavern tales of the Anemo Archon and his lyre are heard across the continent, since taverns are a second home to bards and musicians.
- Language: German appears in names, such as Venti's lyres Der Himmel and Der Frühling. In-game text itself is in English.

Songs and lore: Songs carry Mondstadt's story. A song of resistance was whispered in dark places under Decarabian and later under the corrupt nobility, and became an anthem for the rebels.

- The song of resistance is described in the story text of the sword Freedom-Sworn. It is a drinking song whose verses say that even if someone silences you or takes your sight you can still sing or see another way, and that only the theft of your song and your freedom shall never do. The text says the weak who could not climb the tower sang it from below, and that it spurred on those who did. It names the group before the tower as a youth, a spirit, an archer, a knight and a flame-haired warrior.

- Windblume Ode, a bow from the Invitation of Windblume event, keeps the rebels' greeting of a nameless flower, and says the old rebellion is now remembered in festive jests and in the lilting lyre-tines of histories long gone by.
- The bard of Old Mondstadt: the artifact text of A Note in Spring's Leich says that when Decarabian fell, the bard strummed a tune that belonged to Istaroth to shield the people from the chaos of a god's death, flinging the tower into another time. A mortal body cannot bear a nation's melody, so the bard fell with the tower and his name was lost to the winds of time, until the wind spirit who became Barbatos claimed it.
- Venti's own songs: his profile has him singing both old songs and new ones nobody has heard. One character story is a praise-poem to the West, East and North winds and the animals of Mondstadt, ending with a joking claim that the credit really belongs to the bard who writes the songs.
- Sea and storm: the wiki reports from NPC dialogue that a Church of Favonius family, the ancestors of Vind, were set to watch for storms off the eastern coast, and that Barbatos sang to the sea, after which no more storms came.

Instruments: The lyre is the signature instrument of Mondstadt. The Windsong Lyre, a playable gadget sold during Invitation of Windblume (1.4) and afterwards in Marjorie's shop in Mondstadt, is described as a traditional instrument; its text says Mondstadt has a long-standing tradition of poetry and song and so a long history of making instruments.

- The Holy Lyre der Himmel: a rosewood lyre with a pattern of flowing wind carved on it, once played by Barbatos. In the Prologue's State of the Holy Lyre der Himmel, Venti says it has lost its Anemo power after a thousand years, and Dvalin's Teardrop Crystal restores some of it. The wiki states it is used at Ludi Harpastum and that lending it otherwise needs signed documents from the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative. At the end of the Prologue it is returned to the Church in poor condition; Venti casts an illusion over it so that it seems repaired.
- Der Frühling: Venti's wooden lyre with Cecilia flowers and blue strings, which the glass 'Vision' he carries to avoid suspicion turns into during combat.

Notable bards: Bards shown in the open world and quests:
- Venti, the Windborne Bard (his in-game title), is the best known. He is secretly Barbatos, the Anemo Archon.
- Alfred is a Mondstadt bard who once performed in Liyue. His young daughter fell ill and died while he was away, and he can be found at night in the graveyard behind Favonius Cathedral, singing her favourite nursery rhymes at her grave.
- Sansa performs in front of the fountain in the city plaza and has collected instruments from across Teyvat. She suffers stage fright and stammers; the world quest To the Winds of Freedom helps her gain confidence.

Scene use: Use a bard as colour: a lyre in a tavern, a song in the plaza, a poem sold for a drink. Songs in Mondstadt are about wind, wine, freedom and its history.

- Treat bards as friendly, informal and slightly scruffy, in keeping with a city that values freedom. A bard may ask to be paid in a drink.
- Songs about the dragon, Vennessa and the rebellion are familiar; few listeners know the Anemo Archon is the wandering bard in the crowd.

- Keep the sacred register separate: the Holy Lyre, the Sisters of the Church and Ludi Harpastum are solemn as well as festive.
- Do not invent the words of named songs beyond what the item texts give.

Examples: - A bard waits for cats to leave the plaza before starting, wine cup in hand.
- A young performer mixes up the words of her song and starts again while the crowd cheers her on.
- A traveller at a tavern table retells the legend of the girl who defeated a drake with the help of a bard.

4.comment: Bards and Music of Mondstadt: Bards of Mondstadt
4.content: Bards are a normal part of Mondstadt's life. They wear green or red-and-brown outfits, play lyres, sing for Mora or drinks, and bring poems to the festivals. They preserve the city's legends and songs of resistance. The most famous is Venti, secretly the Anemo Archon Barbatos.

5.comment: Bards and Music of Mondstadt: Alfred the Bard
5.content: Alfred is a Mondstadt bard who used to play in Liyue. His daughter fell ill and died while he was away on a performance, and she had wished to hear his songs. Now he is found at her grave behind the Favonius Cathedral, singing her favourite nursery rhymes at night. He is courteous to strangers and sympathises with anyone parted from family.

6.comment: Bards and Music of Mondstadt: Sansa the Bard
6.content: Sansa is a young bard who performs in front of the fountain in Mondstadt City. She wants to be an exceptional musician and has collected instruments from across Teyvat. Her parents did not approve of the career and she fell out with them over it. She has studied music rigorously, but anxiety makes her stammer and lose her words in front of an audience. After Venti, the Traveler and a cat named Charcoal helped her in the quest To the Winds of Freedom, she stammers much less.

7.comment: Bards and Music of Mondstadt: Holy Lyre der Himmel
7.content: The Church of Favonius keeps the Holy Lyre der Himmel, a rosewood lyre with a flowing-wind pattern that Barbatos played. It is used at Ludi Harpastum, and lending it otherwise needs the signed approval of the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative. In the Prologue it was taken by the Fatui and recovered; Dvalin's Teardrop Crystal restored some of its Anemo power, and it was later returned to the Church in poor condition.

8.comment: Bards and Music of Mondstadt: Song of Resistance
8.content: According to the story text of the sword Freedom-Sworn, a drinking song was sung in cellars, alleys and taverns in the time of Decarabian, and again against the corrupt nobility. Its verses say you can still sing without a tongue and see with your ears without eyes, and that stealing your song and your freedom shall never do. In the tale it was sung by those who could not climb Decarabian's tower. The wiki notes the song may be the one the bard played to break the storm barrier, but this is only implied.

9.content:
Mondstadt Cuisine (also: Mondstadt food, Mondstadter cuisine, Mondstadt dishes, Mondstadt cooking): Mondstadt cooking is simple, hearty country food shaped by the nation's two great loves, wine and song. Apples, potatoes, cheese, butter, milk and cream turn up everywhere. Signature dishes include Mondstadt Hash Browns eaten with jam, peppered Mondstadt Grilled Fish, the festival meat pie called Moon Pie, honey-roasted Sweet Madame and the steak-and-cheese stack "Pile 'Em Up". The famous drink is dandelion wine, followed by apple cider, alcoholic or not. Drinking is a big part of social life, at taverns such as Angel's Share and the Cat's Tail, and the popular restaurant is Good Hunter.

Because wine is central to Mondstadt's economy and identity, alcohol is a defining part of the cuisine rather than a side note: ingredients used in brewing, above all apples, are common in food too.

Practice: Mondstadt's gentle climate, credited to Barbatos's blessing, lets fruit and vegetables flourish: sunsettias and apples are abundant, grapes grow for wine, and carrots and radishes are grown in small gardens at Springvale and the Dawn Winery. Philanemo Mushrooms are not farmed but grow in residential areas and have entered local diets. Milk, butter, cheese and cream are common in recipes, so a dairy industry is implied.

Signature dishes, as item text describes them: the Mondstadt Hash Brown, a fried cake of mashed potato with a little pinecone for crunch, eaten with jam and "loved by people of all ages"; Mondstadt Grilled Fish, fish grilled over moderate fire and sprinkled with pepper; Moon Pie, a "traditional staple", a small meat pie of pickled meat under baked meringue and a fixture of festivals; Sweet Madame, fowl roasted with honey and sweet flowers; and "Pile 'Em Up", originally a dish of steaks, potatoes and cheese. Barbatos Ratatouille is a plain vegetable chowder with a long history, and Sticky Honey Roast is meat in a sweet honey sauce.

Dandelion wine is the nation's most famous drink and the Dawn Winery's signature product. Apple cider, alcoholic and non-alcoholic, comes next; hard ciders of apple and cherry, beer by the tankard and jagerschnapps are also mentioned in dialogue.

Heavy drinking is a social fact, with consequences. Mondstadt has a large drinking culture and relatively many alcoholics. Nimrod talks of the "Four Drunkards" while struggling with the habit himself, and the bartender Charles has to contact Nimrod's wife when he gets out of hand. Diona dislikes alcohol because her father Draff changes when drunk. The Church of Favonius now sends deaconesses to pray over newly built wardrobes after children complained to Grace about drunk fathers stumbling out of them.

Dandelion wine has fans and imitators. Merchants from other nations have tried to learn the Dawn Winery's methods, honestly and otherwise. Connor, the winery's wine maker, describes it as sweetish and refreshing with a rich cereal aroma. Eula's voice-over says aged dandelion wine should technically be poured into a silver goblet, left to breathe for 12 minutes and given ice cubes so that 60% of the ice is submerged, a ritual she refuses to bother with. The community wiki treats Thousand-Wind Wine as the first dandelion wine. Dandelion wine is Venti's favourite wine; the wiki guesses he is the friend who brought bottles when visiting Zhongli, which canon does not state.

Dishes are tied to people: Amber's favourite is the Sticky Honey Roast from Good Hunter, Bennett likes Sweet Madame (which Fischl likes least), and Jean's favourite is the pizza at the Cat's Tail.

Regional variation: Within Mondstadt: the capital leans on taverns and Good Hunter; Springvale supplies game meat to Good Hunter; the Dawn Winery supplies wine and cider from its own orchards and vineyard and sells part of each year's output locally and the rest along the trade route south of the city.

The wiki's Mondstadt dish list also includes "Millhaven's Morning Plate", "Northern Apple Stew", "Northern Smoked Chicken" and "Sunshine Sprat"; canon gives little beyond their in-game descriptions, so do not invent regional traditions for them.

Scene use: Scene use (this project's suggestion): a Mondstadt meal is warm, unfussy and sociable. Put jam beside the hash brown, fruit on the table and a bottle of dandelion wine or a pitcher of cider within reach. Taverns are noisy with bards and regulars; Good Hunter is busy and struggles to keep up with take-out orders. A guest who declines alcohol can be offered apple cider, which has a reputation as a sobering last drink of the night.

Keep the winery's pride and Diluc's own habits straight: he holds the wine trade but is not fond of wine himself, and asked the winery to develop non-alcoholic drinks so people who cannot drink can still join in. Do not have ordinary Mondstadters know that the bard drinking dandelion wine in the corner is Barbatos.

10.content:
The signature product of the Dawn Winery and Mondstadt's best-known specialty, said to be sweetish, refreshing and rich in cereal aroma. It is Venti's favourite. Thousand-Wind Wine is held to have been the first. Fans compare its strength to absinthe, but canon gives no figure.

Foreign merchants have tried to copy it; Dawn Orchard furnishing text and the quest "Wine, with a Taste of Freedom" touch on attempts to learn the winery's methods. Eula's voice-over describes how aged dandelion wine should technically be served (silver goblet, 12 minutes to breathe, ice 60% submerged) and says she will not bother.

11.content:
A tavern in Mondstadt City established and funded by the Dawn Winery; the bartender is Charles. He says the name refers to the portion of liquor that barrels absorb and distillation evaporates, which brewers call "the share of angels". It once held a monopoly over Mondstadt's wine trade. It sells drinks such as Apple Cider and does not accept tabs (Diluc's story quest).

Its occasional bartending academy was restricted to non-alcoholic drinks after an attendee mixed a drink of three hard liquors (limited-time event "Of Drink A-Dreaming").

12.content: A tavern owned by Margaret, famed for its cats and for Diona, its bartender, whose drinks are said to taste delicious whatever the ingredients. Her arrival ended the monopoly Angel's Share held; Elzer tried to headhunt her and got bitten. It also serves pizza, Jean's favourite when she has time to order one, and has become a gathering place for card players.

13.content: The most popular restaurant in Mondstadt City apart from the tavern, with the waitress Sara. It stresses local ingredients: meat from Springvale hunters and homegrown Mondstadt apples. Sara says it is known for venison steak and satisfying salad, and its daily recommendation board advertises a cold cut platter. Take-out is so popular that the service is understaffed (quest "Food Delivery").

14.content:
A freshly squeezed, fashionable, fruity non-alcoholic drink (per the item text), reputed to sober people up and often ordered as the last of the night. In Diluc's character story the Dawn Winery developed several non-alcoholic drinks at his request, which pleased those who could not drink but wished to join in; the cider's monthly sales rival dandelion wine. Hard ciders also exist.

The story adds that some think Diluc never drinks the public beverages because his standards are so high; the text leaves the reason open.

15.content: A traditional Mondstadt staple: a small meat pie of pickled meat under baked meringue, tied in item text to harvest festivals. Its recipe appears in game from version 1.1.

16.content:
Daily Life in Mondstadt (also: Mondstadt customs, Mondstadter way of life, Life in Mondstadt): Mondstadt is a laid-back city-state of farms, windmills, vineyards and taverns where freedom, wine and song are the shared ideals. No monarch rules it. The Knights of Favonius keep order, the Church of Favonius handles worship, and the Adventurers' Guild takes on odd jobs. Ordinary life is peaceful, social and open to outsiders.

The mild climate under Barbatos' blessing, the high literacy and the lack of strong social rank make Mondstadt feel informal. People talk to each other freely and strangers such as the Traveler are welcomed. Wine is both the main industry and the main weakness of the city.

Under the easy surface there is real friction: heavy drinking harms some families and the Church can do little about it. Mondstadters are also open to the unusual, as their acceptance of Eula, of Albedo's alchemy and of Durin shows.

Practice: - **Work.** Farming, winemaking, hunting, smithing, trading and serving in taverns are the usual trades. Apples, grapes and sunsettias are plentiful, and most farms have a windmill.
- **Drink.** Dandelion wine and apple cider are the best-known drinks. Alcohol is part of social life, from the Angel's Share tavern to family dinners.
- **Order.** The Knights patrol the city and countryside, settle disputes and fight hilichurls. Most people expect help from them rather than fear them.

- **Education.** Most people are tutored rather than schooled, and those who choose a trade apprentice to a master, like Schulz with the smith Wagner or Sucrose and Timaeus with Albedo. Mondstadters are generally literate. Razor, raised by wolves, is the one known present-day exception.
- **Gliding.** Many people enjoy gliding with a Wind Glider. By the wiki's account a licence is required, taken after an exam with a fee that can sometimes be waived. Instructors such as Amber teach, and serious violations can cost a glider their licence. Springvale's low houses make it a popular practice ground.

- **Library.** The city's library was once the largest in northern Teyvat. After the Great Fire of Fall Equinox, at an unknown date, only a sixth of it remained, and people still read there.
- **Homes.** The city is built in a half-timbered, Gothic style; villages have smaller country houses. Fireplaces are less necessary because the climate stays moderate, but house styles have not changed much.
- **Symbolism.** The rose stands for keeping secrets, not love, in Mondstadt: as wine bottles are corked, so are lips sealed.
- **Social rank.** Class differences have been small since the aristocracy ended long ago. A few families with long lineages, such as the Gunnhildr and Ragnvindr, still have good reputations, but this brings respect rather than privilege.
- **Agriculture.** Fresh fruit and grapes are plentiful, and carrots and radishes grow in small gardens at Springvale and the Dawn Winery. Philanemo mushrooms grow near homes and are part of the local diet. Dairy foods show up in recipes even though cattle are never seen.
- **Alcohol and families.** Nimrod, a relapsing drinker, mentions the "Four Drunkards" as the city's biggest drinkers; his wife Eury and Sister Victoria worry, and the bartender Charles contacts Eury when Nimrod drinks too much. Diona dislikes alcohol because her father Draff changes when he is drunk, though she does not link his behaviour to his drinking. After children complained to Grace about drunk fathers stumbling out of wardrobes, deaconesses began blessing newly built wardrobes. Confessors like Victoria are frustrated that prayer cannot address the cause.
- **Trade.** Wine is the main export. The Dawn Winery has over a thousand years of history and is the best-known supplier, and outsiders have tried, honestly and not, to learn how its dandelion wine is made. Liyue merchants buy alcohol and resell it elsewhere, usually arriving through the Stone Gate, while foreign visitors mostly dock at Dornman Port. Dornman Port itself is less developed because it was built inside ruins.
- **Travel.** The Adventurers' Guild's Teyvat Travel Highlights (author unknown) describe a visiting bard who met Guild members often on the road, and whose packing list includes a tent, maps, rations and a first-aid kit.

Regional variation: - **Mondstadt City.** On an island in Cider Lake, with a central plaza, the Cathedral and the Knights' headquarters. Busy market streets and taverns.
- **Springvale and the Dawn Winery.** Rural life: hunting, orchard work, vegetable gardens and glider practice at Springvale, vineyards and cellars at the winery.
- **Dornman Port.** The trading and fishing harbour in the north, more rustic than the city.
- **Wolvendom.** Wild country, not settled life. It is where Razor grew up among wolves.

Rural and city people share the same easy manner. Farms rely on windmills, and many people outside the city live in older and smaller houses.

Politics: Mondstadt has no monarch. Before Vennessa's rebellion the Lawrence Clan governed, first justly and later with greed and arrogance. After the rebellion the Knights of Favonius took over keeping order. Barbatos asked that people be left free, so the Knights do not formally rule, though outsiders such as the Qixing and the Fatui treat them as the ruling party. Their Grand Master is Varka, who took a group of Knights to Nod-Krai; in his absence Jean serves as Acting Grand Master and meets visiting delegations. The Knights are based in the city and patrol the countryside.

Other bodies fill in the gaps: the Church of Favonius hears confessions and leads prayer but has little practical power, the Adventurers' Guild posts commissions, and the Dawn Winery dominates the economy.

Festivals: The year's main festivals are the Windblume Festival (a celebration of the Thousand Winds, about offering windblumes to Barbatos and loved ones; its origins lie in the rebels against Decarabian who used the flower as a code), Ludi Harpastum (fifteen days of food, games and music celebrating Barbatos' gift of wine and freedom) and Weinlesefest (new wine and the return of the Anemo Archon each autumn). Ordinary people take part through cooking, decorating and attending, and each has its own entry.

During Ludi Harpastum, taverns put their best dishes outside, the Dawn Winery sends out barrels of beer and cider, and families hang a handmade Harpastum ball on their door. A visiting bard in the Travel Highlights notes that people have mostly forgotten the festival's sacred origins. A gliding championship is held in the last days. At the Windblume Festival, which wildflower was the "real" Windblume has been forgotten and is a subject of friendly debate.

Scene use: Set scenes in a warm, breezy city: windmills turning, wine and apples at stalls, bards in the plaza, Knights in white armour on patrol and gliders overhead. Mondstadters are friendly, informal and curious about travellers.

- Typical settings are a market street, Angel's Share, a sunny orchard, a farm with a windmill or the library.
- Characters will mention wine, the Knights and the weather far more than rank or ceremony.
- Do not depict a monarch, a strict law code or an official caste system.
- Drinking is common but not harmless; a scene can include a worried family member or a heavy drinker without turning it into a joke.

Treat Varka's absence and the Knights' workload as background, not as a crisis. Keep references at or before Version 7.1 and use only the details above; prices, laws and holidays beyond those here are not established.

Examples: - A Mondstadt stallholder offers apples, says the cider is from the Dawn Winery and suggests Angel's Share for the evening.
- A young glider asks a Knight whether the exam fee for a licence can be waived.
- A deaconess blesses a new wardrobe at a family's request, while a worried confessor admits it will not solve the real problem.

17.comment: Daily Life in Mondstadt: Gliding in Mondstadt
17.content: Gliding with a Wind Glider is a widely loved Mondstadt pastime. According to the community wiki, a licence is required and given after an exam with a fee, and instructors such as Amber give lessons. Violations can bring fines and, in serious cases, licence suspension. Springvale's low houses make it a popular place to practise. A gliding championship is held during Ludi Harpastum.

18.comment: Daily Life in Mondstadt: Drinking Culture
18.content: Alcohol is central to Mondstadt's economy and social life, and a number of people struggle with it. Nimrod mentions the "Four Drunkards" as the city's biggest drinkers, and is himself a relapsing drinker, which worries his wife Eury and Sister Victoria. Diona dislikes alcohol because of her father Draff's changes when drunk. After children told Grace about drunk fathers stumbling out of wardrobes, deaconesses began blessing new wardrobes.

19.comment: Daily Life in Mondstadt: Mondstadt Library
19.content: Once the largest library in northern Teyvat, the Mondstadt Library was reduced to a sixth of its size by the Great Fire of Fall Equinox, at an unknown date. It still holds many books, and people read there.

20.content:
Mondstadt Fashion (also: Mondstadt clothing, Mondstadt attire, Mondstadt uniforms): Mondstadt dress is practical folk clothing. Men wear wide trousers tucked into tall boots, women wear dirndl-style dresses or blouses with bodices, and children dress as small versions of the adults. Distinct uniforms mark bards (green), maids, Church of Favonius sisters (black habits, rarely white) and the Knights of Favonius (black clothing under white plate armour with wing motifs).

Visual design in the wiki is likened to German-speaking regional folk dress, but in-world no text explains the styles; they are simply what Mondstadters wear.

Practice: - Boys: short-sleeved tunics with short vests and short trousers.
- Men: wide trousers tucked into tall boots; several shirt and vest variants exist, including a distinct style for elderly men.
- Girls and women: dirndl-style dresses, often pink or blue for girls and red, orange or blue for women; other women's outfits use detached sleeves, bloomers and short boots.

- Women's variants: the first has a blouse and bodice in white-and-blue, white-and-green or two browns; the second is similar but has no bodice; the third is a double-breasted puff-sleeved jacket over a knee-length dress, either a gray jacket with a blue dress and short gloves or a dark purple jacket with a white dress and long gloves.
- Bards: men wear a green jacket over a white-and-green striped shirt with green trousers, white boots and a green cravat; women wear a white blouse and brown skirt under a red dress. Only one style per gender is known.
- Maids: Mondstadt's maid uniforms are admired abroad; in Liyue, Master Hui had such uniforms made for his servant Xi, who calls it a curious hobby of his.
- Church of Favonius: sisters wear a habit, mostly black, with a white version seen on only a few sisters.

- Knights of Favonius, men: black long-sleeved shirt, riding trousers, gloves and brown leather shoulder pads under white plate armour, in plain or brass-accented versions. Wing motifs decorate the armour and the order's crest sits on the breastplate (on custom uniforms, around the midsection). The sword hangs sheathed at the left hip.
- Knights, women: black long-sleeved shirt, close-fitting trousers and a gray knee-length skirt under white plate armour, with greaves but no knee guards. The sword hangs at the right hip.
- Not every knight carries a sword and only a few carry a blowing horn. The standard sword resembles the Traveler's Handy Sword in shape.
- Kaeya is the noted exception to the crest on his uniform; the shield version of the crest is a shortened form of the uniform one.

Regional variation: Dress here is Mondstadt-specific; visitors from Liyue, Inazuma and elsewhere wear their own styles. The maid uniform is the one local style noted as a foreign fancy.

Scene use: Describe townsfolk in vests, boots and dirndls, knights in white armour with wing motifs, bards in green and sisters in black habits when you need Mondstadt to feel recognisable at a glance.

Do not give meaning to habit colour, researcher outfits or rank markings that canon does not state. Keep descriptions of children's clothing plain and practical.

Examples: - A bard in a green jacket and cravat tunes a lyre outside a tavern.
- A knight on patrol with plate armour over a black shirt, sword at the hip.
- A sister in a black habit crossing the Cathedral square.

21.comment: Mondstadt Fashion: Knights of Favonius Uniform
21.content: Standard Knights dress is a black shirt with trousers (men) or a gray skirt (women), worn under white plate armour decorated with wing motifs and the order's crest on the breastplate. Men carry swords on the left, women on the right. Individual knights may wear custom uniforms, with the crest placed lower on the midsection.

22.comment: Mondstadt Fashion: Church of Favonius Habit
22.content: Sisters of the Church of Favonius wear a habit that is usually black; a white version has been seen on only a few sisters. Canon does not say what the colours signify, and the design for male clergy is not shown.

23.content:
Religion in Mondstadt (also: Mondstadt faith, worship of the Anemo Archon, Barbatos worship, Mondstadt Cathedral worship): Mondstadt worships Barbatos, the Anemo Archon and God of Freedom. Devotion runs through the Church of Favonius and its Cathedral in Mondstadt City, the Statues of the Seven, a few ancient ruined temples and festivals such as Windblume, Ludi Harpastum and Weinlesefest. The faith is relaxed: Barbatos asked for freedom rather than obedience, so people honour him with wine, song and flowers more than strict doctrine. Most worshippers do not know that their god walks the streets as the bard Venti.

The Church of Favonius staffs the Cathedral, the highest landmark in the city, where its sisters pray. According to Jean, the Knights also manage the Church. The Church's most precious holding is the Holy Lyre der Himmel, an instrument said to have belonged to Barbatos himself. Older strata of belief lie beneath this: a faded cult of the Four Winds, and a temple where the Ruler of Time was once honoured beside the Anemo god.

The overall tone is affectionate rather than awed. Mondstadters thank Barbatos for the dandelions, the mild climate and the wine, and the Church is seen more as a civic institution than a force in daily life. The Traveler meets the faith early: Paimon explains the Statues of the Seven and Anemoculi in Mondstadt.

Practice: - Prayer and blessing. Sisters pray at the Cathedral; Seamus Pegg greets people with May the Anemo Archon protect you on your path. Rosaria, the irreverent nun, skips prayers.
- Offerings. People with Visions offer Anemoculi at Statues of the Seven; festivals offer flowers (Windblume), wine (Ludi Harpastum, Weinlesefest).

- The Cathedral. The Favonius Cathedral is run by the Church of Favonius and is used to worship the Anemo Archon. A travel note calls it the city's highest landmark. Its basement holds the Holy Lyre der Himmel, guarded.
- Anemo Archon Statue. In the plaza in front of the Cathedral stands a statue of Barbatos as a hooded figure with two wings and cupped hands. Its pedestal bears a line in the Teyvat script rendered as The Gateway of Celestia.
- Clergy. Known figures include Seneschal Seamus Pegg (the Cardinal of Daybreak), Cardinal Calvin (who covers for him), Deacon Dahlia (Herald of Barbatos), Deaconess Barbara (the Shining Idol), Mother Maria and a number of nuns including Rosaria. The Church's symbol on headwear is a fleur-de-lis variant with wide, downward-curving wings, resembling the Anemo emblem. Sisters wear black habits, or white ones in a few cases; whether colour reflects rank is unknown.
- Everyday ministry. The Church hears confessions and says prayers but has little power over social problems such as heavy drinking; deaconesses even bless new wardrobes after children complained to Grace about drunken fathers stumbling out of them.
- Statue offerings. Anemoculi are consolidated winds that only allogenes such as the Traveler can see. Fairy tales say the statues originally had gem eyes that swallows took, and Anemoculi are offered in exchange for the Seven's blessings. The quest The Blessings of The Seven introduces the custom.

- Ludi Harpastum. A fifteen-day festival of food, games and music that commemorates how Barbatos taught his people to brew wine and live freely. The champion chooses a maiden to throw the Harpastum, a ball wrapped in red cloth, at the end; whoever picks it up is said to enjoy good fortune for a year. The Holy Lyre is used in this festival, and any other use requires signed documents from the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative.
- Windblume. A festival celebrating the thousand winds. People offer windblumes, a flower said to have been a symbol of freedom and resistance in Decarabian's era, to Barbatos and to those they love; love poems often go with them. A Windblume Star, chosen from those who excelled during the festival or sacrificed for Mondstadt, formally presents a flower to Barbatos at the Windblume Ceremony, and individuals may leave flowers at his large statue throughout. The identity of the real windblume has been lost and is a matter of popular debate.
- Weinlesefest. A festival celebrating the return of the Anemo Archon on the west wind each autumn. People brew fresh wine and keep it sealed until Windcoming Day, when it is uncasked as a way of inviting the god to share a drink. If he is satisfied, a gentle breeze blesses the people. The 3.1 event Of Ballads and Brews was set during it.
- Rosaria's attitude. Rosaria avoids prayers and morning mass. She says a god might have the power to protect everyone but would never choose to, and that prayer is for yourself, not for gods or others. Barbara is sure she believes in the Anemo Archon anyway.

Regional variation: Worship is concentrated in Mondstadt City, where the Cathedral gives it a formal home. Elsewhere it is mostly folk custom. The wiki's Venti page says Vennessa appointed the ancestors of Vind, a member of the Church today, to watch the eastern coast and warn Mondstadt of storms, so the Church has long had outposts. The old temples are ruins: the Temple of the Falcon at Windrise and the Temple of the Wolf near Thousand Winds are now explorable sites.

The Falcon domain text calls its ruin a temple devoted to the benevolent Falcon of the West, watching over Windrise for thousands of years. The Wolf domain text says the priests are gone and monsters hold the temple, though the spirit of the Wolf is said to watch over Mondstadt's fields from elsewhere.

History: The oldest faith is that of Arcadia. The Thousand Winds Temple was built by its people for Istaroth, the Ruler of Time. During the Archon War the Gunnhildr Clan, sheltering among the ruins from the blizzards of Decarabian and Boreas, built a small shrine to Istaroth and prayed; their prayers were answered by a small wind spirit, the future Barbatos, who also met Istaroth there and received fragments of her authority. After he became the Anemo Archon the temple was rebuilt for both of them, and the Sacrificial weapons were its ceremonial implements. Istaroth was gradually forgotten for unknown reasons and only Barbatos was worshipped. In the aristocratic period the site became an arena where slaves fought. After Vennessa's rebellion about a thousand years ago the people worshipped the Four Winds and built temples to them; after the cataclysm that worship declined and the temples were abandoned.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Church of Favonius still centres on Barbatos, and no change to Mondstadt's faith has been found in the material checked. Seneschal Seamus Pegg is back in Mondstadt after the Nod-Krai expedition (see his entry), and Dahlia is a playable character (5.7) while remaining a deacon and Barbatos's herald.

Scene use: Keep the faith as gentle background, warm and informal. Do not have Mondstadters preach doctrine or recognise Venti as a god.

A Cathedral scene should feel quiet and slightly formal: stone steps, the plaza statue with its cupped hands, sisters at prayer, and perhaps a visitor asking to see the Holy Lyre and meeting polite paperwork. Characters can talk about the god casually, as a generous presence rather than a stern one.

Clergy meeting a stranger show friendly curiosity without pressure. A character who knows Venti's secret (Varka, Seamus Pegg, Dahlia) should be careful not to expose it. Rosaria is the standard voice of doubt; Barbara the standard voice of sincere, anxious devotion.

24.content:
Barbatos is the Anemo Archon, whom Mondstadt calls the God of Freedom. He does not rule; the Knights of Favonius, not a priest-king, run the city, and the Church of Favonius is his devotional institution. Seamus Pegg's blessing and Jean's battle lines are the most common direct appeals. The public does not connect him with the bard Venti; his origin and his identity as Venti are major spoilers covered in Venti's own entries.

The official map description credits Barbatos with the dandelion scent that drifts across Cider Lake to the city. Weinlesefest tradition says he returns each autumn on the west wind.

25.comment: Religion in Mondstadt: Holy Lyre der Himmel
25.content:
The Church keeps this lyre in the Cathedral basement under guard. Its item description calls it a treasure that once belonged to Barbatos, with its Anemo power run dry. It is used in Ludi Harpastum, and other use needs signed documents from the Grand Master, the Seneschal and a community representative. In the Prologue, Venti cannot borrow it because the Seneschal is away with the expedition, so the Traveler enters the basement at night. After the lyre is retrieved from the Fatui, Venti says it is the real thing but its power has run dry after a thousand years, with a rosewood frame carved with flowing wind. A purified Teardrop Crystal from Dvalin partly restores it. At the end of the Prologue it is returned to Barbara in a worse condition, and Venti masks this with an Anemo illusion.

Venti's other lyre, which his fake Vision turns into in battle, is a separate instrument; the wiki names it Der Fruehling. He does not carry the Holy Lyre himself.

26.comment: Religion in Mondstadt: Statues of the Seven in Mondstadt
26.content:
Mondstadt's Statues of the Seven are the god's shrines in the wild. People with Visions offer them Anemoculi, consolidated winds that only allogenes can see, in exchange for blessings. The Traveler first learns the custom in The Blessings of The Seven, when Paimon explains the offering. Fairy tales say the statues' eyes were gems taken by swallows. Long ago Mondstadt lost a statue of its own, which the Traveler later finds hanging upside down in the ruins in Call of the Abyss.

The statues also revive fallen travellers, heal characters and act as waypoints, and the Traveler can resonate with a statue to change element. These are gameplay features, not liturgy.

27.comment: Religion in Mondstadt: Thousand Winds Temple and Istaroth
27.content:
The ruins northeast of Mondstadt were built by the people of Arcadia for Istaroth, the Ruler of Time. The Gunnhildr Clan prayed there during the Archon War, and a wind spirit, the future Barbatos, answered. Once Barbatos was an Archon the temple was rebuilt for both, and the Sacrificial weapon series served in its rituals; later Istaroth was forgotten. The official map description gives the carved maxim that wind brings the seeds of tales and time lets them take root. Aristocrats later used the amphitheatre for slave combat.

The phrase thousand winds is used across sources for Istaroth, for the personified winds that protect Mondstadt (Venti was once a single thread of them) and in one Aranara usage for erosion. The Windblume Festival is described as a celebration of the thousand winds.

28.comment: Religion in Mondstadt: Four Winds worship
28.content: The Four Winds are the four guardians Barbatos entrusted with Mondstadt's protection before he vanished a thousand years ago. After Vennessa's rebellion Mondstadters worshipped them and built temples; after the cataclysm the worship declined, the temples were abandoned and the Four Winds were almost forgotten. The Temple of the Falcon at Windrise is a ruin devoted to the Falcon of the West, and the Temple of the Wolf is a ruin devoted to the Wolf of the North. Their four symbols still appear on Mondstadt character-card art.

29.comment: Religion in Mondstadt: Herald of Barbatos
29.content: Dahlia, a Church deacon, holds the title Herald of Barbatos and knows that Venti is Barbatos. According to the wiki, Venti appointed him herald when he awoke shortly before the Prologue: Dahlia relays notable events in the nation to Venti, and Venti gives his views back through him. Barbara looks up to him because he shares Barbatos's word, though he rarely stays long in the Cathedral and prefers markets and taverns. Dahlia became playable in 5.7.

30.comment: Religion in Mondstadt: Seamus Pegg and the Church leadership
30.content: Seamus Pegg, the Cardinal of Daybreak, is Seneschal of the Church of Favonius and the father of Jean and Barbara. He comes from Nod-Krai. He joined Varka's expedition, so Cardinal Calvin covered his duties. His absence is why Venti cannot get the Seneschal's signature for the Holy Lyre in the Prologue. The wiki says he is aware of Venti's identity. During the 3.1 event Of Ballads and Brews he was still away with Varka's expedition; after the quest An Elegy for Faded Moonlight he left the expedition for "private matters", and in his own dialogue he says he returned to Mondstadt only as the Nod-Krai conflict drew to a close, intending to take on more of the Church's workload.

key: Festival of the Returning Wind and Fine Wine
31.content:
Weinlesefest (also: Wine Harvest Festival, Festival of the Returning Wind and Fine Wine): Weinlesefest ("wine harvest festival" in German) is held in Mondstadt every autumn, when the west wind returns with the harvest. Citizens brew fresh wine and keep it sealed until Windcoming Day, when it is uncasked to invite the Anemo Archon to share a drink. If the Archon is pleased with the wine, a gentle breeze is summoned to bless the people.

Jean describes it as an ancient festival that began as a welcome for Lord Barbatos's return, alongside Ludi Harpastum and the Windblume Festival, and the most important part of the fall. In the 3.1 event the festival is organised by the Knights of Favonius, the Church of Favonius and the Adventurers' Guild, with its main venue a festival market outside Springvale.

Practice: New wine is brewed and sealed during the harvest season, then opened on Windcoming Day in a toast to the Anemo Archon. A breeze afterwards is read as his blessing.

- Preparations: the harvest season brings a rush of requests to the Adventurers' Guild, mostly deliveries and escorts of goods, and the Knights plan the festival ahead.
- Venue (as shown in the 3.1 event): a festival market with stalls, a stage and a Knights of Favonius charity shop; Angel's Share runs a stall there.
- Sealing: Jean says households once brewed fresh wine each year and kept it sealed at least until Windcoming Day of the following year's Weinlesefest.
- Toast: on Windcoming Day everyone gathers at the market for a toasting ceremony, and a bard sings before the wines are opened. Wine may be offered to the Archon.

Wines are made with whatever ingredients their makers choose, so no two brews taste alike. Jean adds that the festival is when Mondstadters living away often come home, and when those who cannot return miss family most; in 3.1 the Knights used the market to raise funds for needy children and elderly people. The event's closing scene shows several Mondstadters spending the festival with family or remembering family members who mattered to them.

The event: In the limited event Of Ballads and Brews (3.1), the Traveler and Paimon help Razor, whose lost parents left him a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine. They gather ingredients for his own bottle. Bennett gives Small Lamp Grass for the Adventurers' Guild's explorer's courage, Rosaria gives Mist Flower Corolla for the Church's tender and true love, and Noelle and Sucrose supply Quadruple-Sweetness Sunsettia for the Knights' defender's will. Diluc provides a barrel, Diona mixes the brew, and Venti adds Dandelion Seeds last to catch the wind's memory. Razor's wine is buried under the great tree at Windrise, and Razor says he will open it with everyone once he is grown up. The next day is Windcoming Day, when the toast is held with other wines, including bottles Bennett and Klee brought as an offering.

Venti sings "Thousand-Wind Wine" at the toast. Klee first worries that the Archon did not come because she feels no wind, but the wind rises soon after, with Venti quietly using his power. Razor smells his parents' bottle and sees a vision of them, adventurers sharing the wine on a cliff and choosing his name. The event also had gameplay phases (Autumn Crisis, Highwind Trial, Charity and Creativity, Fecund Blessings) and gave the weapon Missive Windspear.

Scene use: Use it for warm autumn scenes: stalls at Springvale, barrels, fruit carts, a stage with music and the question of whether the wind will come. It suits quiet talks over wine and family reminiscence.

A character may put a bottle aside for Windcoming Day, argue about the best ingredients, or simply wait to feel the first breeze. Anyone can brew their own wine for the occasion.

Do not state that Venti caused the wind unless the speaker is Venti or someone he told; most Mondstadters take the breeze as the Archon's answer.

Examples: - A brewer seals a cask of new wine and writes the day it will be opened.
- A courier hurries fruit carts to the market while hilichurls lurk on the road.

- A child asks whether the Archon dislikes the wine when no wind blows; an adult replies that he may come in other forms.

32.content: The day on which wine sealed during the harvest is uncasked, as a symbolic invitation for the Anemo Archon to share a drink. If he approves the wine, a gentle breeze blesses the people. In the 3.1 event it is the day after the group buries Razor's wine.

33.content: Lisa says it was, so they say, the first kind of wine Mondstadters learned to make; Venti calls it the original Dandelion Wine. It tastes different from brew to brew, because everyone is free to add what they like, which makes it impractical to sell, so it is almost never seen in markets or taverns. Venti says dandelion seeds should be added at the last moment to capture the wind and keep its memory in the wine. Lisa judges that Razor's parents brewed the bottle they left him.

34.content:
Windblume Festival (also: Windblume): The Windblume Festival is Mondstadt's once-yearly festival of love and freedom, and Klee calls it the city's biggest celebration. The city is decorated, and people offer Windblumes to the Anemo Archon Barbatos and to anyone they love or admire. Gifts and love poems can go with them, but the flowers are not only romantic. People also use the festival to mend or deepen any relationship. "Windblume" (German for "wind flower") began as a secret code word among the rebels against the tyrant god Decarabian. Today nobody agrees which flower the Windblume really is.

Each year one person is named the Windblume Star and offers a Windblume of their choice to Barbatos for all of Mondstadt at the Windblume Ceremony. Custom says everyone should do things for themselves during the festival, so there are far fewer commissions. The Adventurers' Guild has little work to give out.

Practice: People offer Windblumes informally at the great statue of Barbatos all through the festival, and give flowers to loved ones. Florists such as Flora have more customers than they can handle.

- Do it yourself: Venti says the festival belongs both to the Anemo Archon and to every Mondstadter looking for love, and anyone who wants love must do everything themselves. Many people also use the time to settle matters of the heart. Katheryne and shopkeepers turn away offers of help, and Marjorie of the souvenir shop laughs at the idea.
- The Windblume Star: the Star is someone who has truly proven themselves during the festival or made great sacrifices for Mondstadt. Acting Grand Master Jean announces the choice and attends the ceremony with them.
- Festivities: taverns sell limited-edition wines (Venti names Applebloom Cider and saves his Mora for them). There are games, balloons, music and decorations across the city and at Statues of The Seven such as Windrise, Starfell Lake and the Dawn Winery.

- Love poems are a festival habit. Wordsmiths can even sell lessons in writing them, as Venti did.
- Cape Oath is a popular date spot.
- The Adventurers' Guild treats the festival as a recruiting opportunity. Branch Master Cyrus sends adventurers to look for traces of the Windblume in Stormterror's Lair, and says the festival should carry on the rebellious spirit of the heroes who resisted Decarabian.

Origins: In Old Mondstadt, Decarabian ruled from his tower. People who planned to overthrow him used "Windblume" as their secret sign. The festival grew out of that rebellion; when it was first held is unknown.

The original Windblume was a nameless, "floaty" flower from the dreams of Decarabian's people. It was said to thrive in the harshest wind and cold and to root more firmly the harder the wind blew, which is why the rebels made it their symbol. Venti confirms that the word dates from Old Mondstadt and was a code word for keeping in touch and resisting in secret. Few people today remember this meaning.

The weapon text of Windblume Ode keeps the old greeting in spirit: the rebels offered each other "this nameless flower" and hoped for the day the storms would stop. It names the forgotten red-haired warrior, who turned away from the newborn god after the victory, as the first to pass the sign. It links the Windblume to his descendants, the Ragnvindr Clan, who keep bringing light in dark times. In peacetime, the text says, the flower came to mean love and gladness, which is surely what those rebels wanted. Few people know about the Ragnvindr link.

The windblume: During the limited event Invitation of Windblume (1.4), the city argued about which flower is the "true" Windblume. Most people favour the dandelion; others name the Windwheel Aster, which Mondstadters call "the visible winds."

The two big camps are the Dandelionites, the most popular, who see the dandelion as the Windblume and the festival as one for lovers, and the Asterists ("Windblume Traditionalists"), who choose the Windwheel Aster and say the festival should remember Old Mondstadt's liberation. The guard Lawrence and the scholar Dr. Edith describe them. Other candidates in that festival included the Cecilia (Beatrice's pick), the Sweet Flower, Small Lamp Grass and the Wolfhook (Razor and Bennett's). Sucrose took an alchemically recreated giant Sweet Flower from antiquity, the "Tetratanic Sweet Flower," as her own.

Regional variation: In Springvale, young hunters looking for love go into Wolvendom during the festival to catch foxes, then release them with flower wreaths on their heads. The hunter Allan admits he failed to catch one last year and doubts he will this time. Mentioned in event dialogue (1.4, 3.5).

Depictions: Festivals shown in limited events:
- Invitation of Windblume (1.4): Venti runs a paid love-poem class (Kaeya, Timaeus and Bennett among the students) and the Traveler helps him collect the poems. The Traveler is chosen Windblume Star and offers their chosen flower at the statue with Jean. Afterwards Venti and the Traveler tidy the wind currents of Stormterror's Lair as a gift for Dvalin, who soon flies past.
- Windblume's Breath (3.5): the Knights name Sucrose Windblume Festival Special Ambassador, to do good deeds for people. With the Traveler and Collei, who is visiting from Sumeru, she chases a riddle-slip found in the children's book "The Boar Princess." It leads to the Lantern of Utmost Joy on a floating island above Falcon Coast, a Hexenzirkel device that connects Klee's mother Alice and Scarlett with the finders. The "supreme blessing" turns out to be the joy of being with friends.

Recent: The Archon Quest Paralogism (Interlude Chapter Act IV, 5.6) takes place as a new Windblume Festival begins. Under cover of the festival, the Knights stage the trial of Albedo to expose creatures born of Durin's lingering life force, and then defend Mondstadt against their attack on the city. When the festival opens, Jean names Venti the Windblume Star. He sings while Albedo's alchemy turns Mini Durin into a human, reborn in place of the fallen dragon.

Scene use: Use it for light-hearted Mondstadt scenes: decorated streets, flower stalls, music, wine, couples at Cape Oath, people working up courage to give someone flowers. Shopkeepers and the Guild may turn down offers of help, saying people do things themselves at Windblume.

Arguments over the "real" Windblume make easy small talk. A traditionalist may say the festival is about freedom from Decarabian rather than romance. Windblumes need not be romantic: friends, family, mentors and the Archon all receive them.

Mondstadters revere Barbatos at the festival but do not know the bard Venti is their god. Jean naming Venti as Windblume Star in 5.6 does not mean the public knows. Keep the tone affectionate rather than solemn: Windblume Ode notes that the old rebellion is now remembered through festive jests.

Examples: - A young knight leaves an unsigned bouquet of dandelions and a love poem for someone at the office.
- A couple asks a strict parent for approval by offering him a Windblume.
- An Asterist spends the festival quietly outside the city, remembering the rebels of Old Mondstadt.

- A bard sells love-poem lessons to fund his wine.
- A fan club builds a giant flower sculpture for its idol (Barbara's fans did this in 1.4).

35.comment: Windblume Festival: Windblume Star and Windblume Ceremony
35.content: At the Windblume Ceremony, held in the plaza before the great statue of Barbatos, the year's Windblume Star offers a Windblume of their own choosing to the Anemo Archon for all of Mondstadt. The Star is someone who has truly proven themselves during the festival or made great sacrifices for the city. The Acting Grand Master announces the choice and attends the ceremony. Known Stars: the Traveler (shown in the 1.4 event) and Venti (in the 5.6 Archon Quest Paralogism). Many townsfolk wonder aloud who will get the honour.

36.content: These are the two main schools of thought on the "true" Windblume. Dandelionites, the larger group, say it is the dandelion and that the Windblume Festival is for lovers. Asterists, or Windblume Traditionalists, say it is the Windwheel Aster ("the visible winds") and that the festival should remember Old Mondstadt's liberation from Decarabian. Most people have forgotten that meaning, so the Asterists are a minority. Some people hold neither view. Barbatos refuses to settle the question.

37.comment: Windblume Festival: Lantern of Utmost Joy
37.content: During the Windblume Festival of the event Windblume's Breath (3.5), a "prophecy" slip tucked into a children's book sent Sucrose, Collei and the Traveler looking for "a flower not of this world, a guide who never gets lost, one who would never lie and a legend that never ends." The answers lit the Lantern of Utmost Joy on Hexenzirkel's Island in the Sky above Falcon Coast. The witches had left the lantern in Barbatos's care, and lighting it put the group in contact with Alice and Scarlett. The island became permanently accessible after Paralogism (5.6).
